lead: Naperville plumbing deals with cold winters, a high water table and basements in homes from the 1970s on. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Naperville.
risk: sump pump failures, frozen pipes and water heater replacement
risk_short: sump pumps, frozen pipes and water heaters
why: Most Naperville homes were built from the 1970s through the 2000s, and nearly all have basements with sump pumps. A high water table means sump pumps run often, and a failure can flood a basement fast.
The Historic District has older homes with galvanized supply lines. Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and hose bibs.
utility: City of Naperville Water Utility (Lake Michigan water through the DuPage Water Commission)
water: Naperville buys Lake Michigan water treated by Chicago and piped through the DuPage Water Commission. It is moderately hard.
tips: Add a battery backup to your sump pump.
Test your sump pump each spring.
Replace water heaters past 10 to 15 years.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Naperville, the Historic District, Cress Creek, Ashbury, Tall Grass, White Eagle and every other Naperville neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Naperville Transportation, Engineering and Development Business Group, and plumbers must be licensed by the Illinois Department of Public Health.

faq.q: Why do Naperville sump pumps run so often?
faq.a: Much of DuPage County has a high water table, so groundwater collects around basement foundations. The sump pump removes it. A battery backup keeps it running in a power outage.
